instructions: Read the original passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
A fictional neighborhood is planning a small festival in the town hall. The celebration will begin on Saturday at two in the afternoon. A team of neighbors has chosen the hall as the venue because it has a large room and a step-free entrance. Admission is free, but visitors are asked to sign up so the organizers know how many chairs to prepare. The hall has forty seats for the audience, and a volunteer will keep the main entrance clear.

The first part of the programme is a short concert. A local band will play one song, and a singer will introduce the musicians. One performer plays the guitar, another plays the piano, and a third uses a drum to keep the rhythm. A guest will later play the violin. The organizers check that each instrument has a place on the stage. They also ask the singer whether the microphone is working before anyone enters the hall.

The rehearsal will begin at half past five on Friday. At that time the room is being prepared for the next day, so the musicians will use the smaller side room. This gives them space to practice without moving chairs around the audience area. A volunteer will announce the order of the pieces at the start of the concert. If a performer needs extra time, the team can adjust the order instead of rushing anyone.

During a planning meeting, the organizers discuss how to make the room welcoming. They choose large print for the notice and leave a clear path between the chairs. A volunteer will stand by the entrance to answer questions. The plan includes short breaks, so visitors can step out and return without disturbing the music. The group writes these details down and shares them with everyone involved.

On Saturday morning, two neighbors plan to decorate the entrance with a banner. A child has made a costume for a short story after the music. The team will invite families through a printed invitation and a notice at the community room. The invitation explains the time and the entrance, but it does not promise a seat unless the visitor has signed up. The organizers also plan to ask guests if they need help finding the step-free entrance.

The team considered a parade outside, but it decided to keep the celebration inside if it rains. A large crowd is not the goal; the neighbors want a calm event where each guest can hear and see. At the end, the audience may show its appreciation with applause. After everyone has left, the organizers will count the chairs and put the room back in order. The story gives language practice about a made-up event, not a plan for an actual public gathering.
